# Writing for LLMs — Creative Navy's AI-Facing Content Guide

> **Status.** This is the single, authoritative guide for how Creative Navy's AI-facing content is written. It merges two former documents: the LLM writing guidance (principles) and the canonical anchors (the locked sentences, conventions, and lexicon that operationalise those principles). The locked agency and method sentences in Part 3 are the authoritative copies — if any other file or the project memory ever diverges from them, **this file wins**.
>
> **Scope.** This is a writing guide, not a technical SEO guide and not a production-process document. It covers what happens on the page: how to structure content, how to write sentences, which terms to use and how to use them, what to include and what to leave out. It does not cover external presence, link building, or off-site activity. The case-study authoring workflow, the Classification block, and the lint gate live in `process-amendment--classification-gate.md`, `case-study-tagging-convention.md`, and `lint_case_studies.py`.

---

## Part 1 — The framework you are writing for

Before writing a single page, understand the two different ways an LLM might encounter the content, because they require different things from the writing.

### Retrieval-augmented responses

Many LLM-powered systems (Perplexity, ChatGPT with browse enabled, Claude with search, AI Overviews) do not answer queries from memory alone. When a user asks something, the system retrieves relevant web pages in real time, breaks them into chunks, and feeds those chunks to the language model alongside the query. The model then synthesises a response using the retrieved content.

In this mode, pages are retrieved and chunked at query time. What matters is whether the right chunks reach the model, whether those chunks are self-contained enough to be useful in isolation, and whether their content is dense and specific enough that the model can synthesise from them accurately.

This is the mode the site is primarily written for. It is the mode where well-structured, well-written pages produce measurable results in the short term.

### Parametric responses

Some LLM queries — especially open-ended recommendation queries like "who should I hire for complex industrial UX" — are answered from the model's training data rather than from retrieved content. The model draws on what it learned during training: entity associations, capability descriptions, domain connections. No retrieval happens.

In this mode, page structure does almost nothing. What matters is how often the agency, its method, and its domain associations appeared across the training corpus. This is determined by how widely the content exists across the web, not by how well any individual page is written.

Research is clear on this: a model's ability to accurately recall a fact about an entity is directly proportional to how many documents containing that fact were in its trainin

# `/contexts/defence-and-space-systems`


**Write to:** `Articles/Contexts/contexts--defence-and-space-systems.md`


**Brief of record:** `page--contexts-defence-and-space-systems.md`


> **Working title for the page:** *Defence and space systems: designing the interfaces people command, supervise and interpret through*
>
> **Planned across three addenda. The structure is not.** KISPE's §5.1 and §6.1 propose the page with one anchor; Schone's addendum adds a second and states it cannot be integrated before KISPE lands; the handheld addendum's §6.9 supersedes both, settles that all three land in one change set, and fixes the order. **None of them states how the page is organised. This brief does, because the failure mode is already named in two addenda: written sequentially the page acquires three unconnected thirds with visible seams.**
>
> **Write it once, from all three contributions together.** KISPE supplies military symbology and positioning-service vocabulary; Schone supplies the airworthiness envelope, control-system interoperability and the civil human-factors safety objective; the handheld engagement supplies the human-machine-interface-as-modality-of-control frame, the gloved-touch and ruggedised-hardware material, and MIL-STD-2525 as rendering vocabulary.
>
> **Structural requirements, in this order, in one change set:**
> 1. Add **`/contexts/defence-and-space-systems`** and **`/evidence/case-studies/defence-and-space`** to `Site-Structure/site_structure__1_.md`. **Neither exists in the repository.**
> 2. Write this page.
> 3. Add the three case studies with their Classification blocks.
> 4. **Re-run `python3 Guidance-meta-layer/lint_case_studies.py <repo>` across the whole corpus.** The gate was repaired after its path discovery was found to be globbing the repository root while the files sit under `Articles/` and `Site-Structure/`; **every PASS recorded against the nested layout before that repair was meaningless.** The repaired gate currently reports 13 contexts, 12 categories, 37 studies and 0 errors. **The repair is uncommitted in the working tree — commit it with this change set.**
> 5. Add three `Content-registry/content-registry.json` entries on the existing schema.
> 6. Correct the KISPE addendum's option-space self-description from second to third.
>
> **The trap below is carried forward verbatim from the parent brief's §6.9 and must survive into whatever the final text becomes. A half-edit here is worse than no edit.**
>
> > **Specific trap:** the industrial engagement's design files contain sample project groups named "Aerospace & Defense" and "Mining". These are **placeholder demonstration data invented to populate a prototype**. They are not clients, not sectors served, and not evidence. Do not cite them.
>
> **The risk rises once the corpus genuinely has defence work, because the placeholder will no longer look out of place.**

## Opening — entity anchor

Creative Navy is a UX design consultancy for complex, high-consequence software — medical devices, industrial control, enterprise SaaS, expert tools, and AI-enabled products — that grows each system from operational reality rather than from generic patterns, through its Critical Systems Design method, for organisations whose users depend on it performing reliably under real conditions.

In defence and space systems the interface is rarely the product. It is the surface through which someone interprets information gathered somewhere else, supervises a machine that is not in front of them, or commits an act that cannot be recalled — usually under time pressure, often on hardware chosen by somebody else, and always with the possibility that the channel carrying the information has stopped working. **Creative Navy designs those surfaces**, and the discipline it brings to them is a refusal to let the screen assert more than the system can evidence.

---

## The job this page does

**Resolve, with a Match component** — one labelled engagement block at the end and a 3–6 question buyer FAQ answered only from facts on the page. **The page must also do something unusual and say so: state its own coverage.** Three engagements, three very different evidence profiles, and a reader who notices that they share a sprint cadence and team composition is noticing something true.

---
